holidays.name: National Bittersweet Chocolate with Almonds Day
holidays.description: A day to unwrap a bar of dark chocolate studded with crunchy almonds and indulge in the perfect balance of bitter and sweet. Snack lovers everywhere justify it as a health food because of the cocoa and nuts.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial American food holiday that appeared on food-observance calendars, with no single known founder. It follows the pattern of many candy days that celebrate classic confection pairings.
holidays.funFact: Almonds are technically seeds of a fruit related to peaches and cherries, not true nuts, so this chocolate treat is basically a stone-fruit seed bar.

holidays.name: International Day of Radiology
holidays.description: A day celebrating X-rays, MRIs, and the medical professionals who see right through us, literally. It highlights the role of medical imaging in modern healthcare.
holidays.origin: It is observed on November 8 in honor of the anniversary of Wilhelm Röntgen's 1895 X-ray discovery, and the observance is often celebrated in the surrounding days. It was established by the European Society of Radiology, the Radiological Society of North America, and the American College of Radiology.
holidays.funFact: Röntgen's first medical X-ray image was of his wife Anna Bertha's hand, complete with her wedding ring. She reportedly said, 'I have seen my death.'

holidays.name: Hug a Bear Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate all things bear, from teddy bears to cuddly bear-shaped pillows. Please note that hugging actual bears is strongly discouraged and may result in a very bad day.
holidays.origin: This is a lighthearted unofficial observance spread through quirky holiday calendars and social media. It encourages people to show affection to plush companions and to appreciate real bears from a respectful distance.
holidays.funFact: The teddy bear was named after President Theodore Roosevelt after a 1902 hunting trip in which he refused to shoot a captured bear.

holidays.name: Great American Smokeout Week Kickoff Vibes: Quit-Something Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for dropping one bad habit, whether it's doomscrolling, nail biting, or hitting snooze eleven times. The idea is to pick something small and give it up for just 24 hours.
holidays.origin: It riffs on the American Cancer Society's Great American Smokeout, held the third Thursday of November, which began in the 1970s. Habit-quitting challenges have since spread across social media in early November.
holidays.funFact: The first Smokeout in 1971 began when a Massachusetts man, Arthur Mullaney, asked people to give up cigarettes for a day and donate the savings to a high school.
